status_reasoning: Reviewers raise concerns about the collagen secretion experiments, noting 'there is no known cargo of this type' and questioning whether the measurements reflect 'new collagen versus previously secreted collagen.' They request clarification on collagen half-life and proper experimental controls to distinguish newly secreted collagen, indicating uncertainty about whether the data support the claims about normal collagen transport through stapled Golgi.

Reviewers question whether 'stapling results in a dead Golgi' with 'a transient block in traffic at the time of drug addition,' requesting data on collagen half-life compared to staples. They also question co-transfection assumptions, stating 'the experiments assume the cells are co-transfected' and requesting measurement of 'the degree of co-transfection,' indicating uncertainty about whether the Golgi remains fully functional.

Reviewers note that 'some staples may be in cis and others trans' and request this be mentioned in the text. This aligns with the manuscript's acknowledgment that cis-interactions 'cannot be ruled out,' but reviewers want explicit discussion of the heterogeneity in staple localization, indicating this aspect needs clarification.

Reviewers question the interpretation of experiments with soluble and membrane FM proteins, asking 'how much FM protein was actually expressed?' and stating 'a Western blot is needed' because 'a plasmid ratio is given but this isn't particularly helpful in determining the actual protein ratio.' This indicates uncertainty about whether the observed segregation and differential transport reflect physiological conditions or are artifacts of expression levels.
